LESSON: SIGN READING 2.2.1 PRE-READING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.2: Sign Reading 2.2.1 Pre-reading
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 1

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 2.2.1 Pre-reading, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: How do people sit when reading? 2. How do people place books and newspapers while reading?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 2.2.1 Pre-reading together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and Collaboration: Teamwork is nurtured as the learner, in pairs, observe each other’s sitting posture and give feedback.

Values:
• Unity: Cooperation is nurtured as learners observe each other’s sitting posture and give feedback.

• Responsibility is developed as the learner takes care of the reading materials.

Pertinent Contemporary Issues:

Life skills: self-awareness is enhanced as the learner observes appropriate posture in preparation for reading.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Sign reading skill is applied in all learning areas.

Suggested Learning Resources

Manual alphabet chart, flash cards, internet, posters, online dictionaries, assistive devices fitted with appropriate technologies such as hearing aids and

amplifiers, adapted course books, flash cards, sign language dictionary, internet, signed audio-visual recordings.
